q1_issues.issue: The definite common-noun oblique object "the new-moon spring tide" is encoded as the bare constant new_moon_spring_tide instead of minting a witness with its kind atom, which the oblique-object NP rule requires for an article-marked NP.

(Inheritance new_moon_spring_tide tide) puts in a class position the very symbol statement 12 uses as an individual time filler, violating the individual-vs-class discipline that reserves Inheritance for kind/property on both sides.

q2_gaps: a temporal adjunct headed by "at" whose object is a definite common-noun event NP ("at the new-moon spring tide") — the Time role is specified for deictic constants, dates and clock terms, and event-noun time anchors are covered only for before/after ordering
a non-Gregorian day-of-year date ("day 525 of Year 2") — the calendar terms assume a Year/Month/Day decomposition, and nothing says whether a bare day-of-year count belongs in the (Day <n>) slot
notes: The rest of the passage is clean: the copular-with-time-modifier dual-emit, the collective "harvest party" (Member + GroupOf + Cardinality, no distribution rule), the unspecified-scale bucket Measure, and the no-Name treatment of "the Council" all follow the instruction set. "The next morning" emits only the day-part plus Before, which the anaphoric-time rule licenses when the antecedent event carries no day terms, though the passage's own day 525 arguably made day 526 recoverable.
